synopsis: NVIDIA Isaac Sim is a general robotics simulator, open source under Apache 2.0 since version 5.0, with version 6.1 reaching general availability on 15 September 2026 [f8477, f8478, f8481]. Its capabilities include RTX lidar and radar, cameras, ROS 2 integration and neural rendering; the asset library lists 25 RTX lidar models but only one radar model [f8478, f8479, f8480]. AgriGen demonstrated large agricultural scene generation in September 2026, but the research did not verify Isaac Sim or find construction/mining validation or validation for off-road collision warning [f3788, f5850, f5851, f8491]. Sensor credibility remains a qualification gap: ultrasonic sensing is a PhysX ray-cast range model rather than an acoustic model, while RTX sensor crashes and severe multi-sensor frame-rate losses motivate workload-specific benchmarking [f8548, f8488, f8875]. The core is free for internal R&D, but separate asset/component terms apply and redistribution with Omniverse Kit requires NVIDIA AI Enterprise at an undiscovered price; staff statements describing free use for teams of up to two leave the scope of free use needing clarification [f8483, f8484, f8485, f8486]. An in-house open-source chain offers low license cost but high internal labor, and validated radar and qualification-ready Chrono-to-Isaac heavy-machine coupling still require major work [f16128, f9275, f9280].
